sentence: For decades, the best microscopes couldn't tell.
claim: Conventional light microscopes resolve down to about 200 nm; the synaptic cleft (about 10–50 nm) is far smaller, so it could not be seen until electron microscopy in the 1950s.
source_title: Why the synaptic cleft needs an electron microscope (Nagwa explainer)
note: Excerpts: Abbe's limit gives light microscopy about 200 nm lateral resolution; the cleft is 10–50 nm, too small for conventional microscopes; electron microscopes resolve far finer. 'For decades': from Cajal and Golgi's work in the 1880s–1900s to the electron micrographs of 1954–55 (c7).

sentence: Each one reaches out to thousands of others.
claim: A neuron typically forms thousands of connections (synapses).
source_title: Billions of neurons, trillions of synapses (UCLA Brain Research Institute, Brain Fact)
note: Excerpt: about 86 billion neurons, 'each forming thousands of connections'. Some estimates run up to 10,000 per neuron.

sentence: Your brain holds about a hundred trillion of these meeting points.
claim: The human brain has an estimated 100 trillion synapses.
source_title: Billions of neurons, trillions of synapses (UCLA Brain Research Institute, Brain Fact)
note: Excerpt: 'resulting in an estimated 100 trillion synapses'. Estimates range about 100–500 trillion; neocortex counts give about 150–164 trillion (Pakkenberg; Synapse 2001). 'About a hundred trillion' is the commonly cited estimate; the readout says 'about'.

sentence: Camillo Golgi saw one continuous web.
claim: Camillo Golgi supported the reticular theory: the nervous system as one continuous network.
source_title: Meet the Nobels: Golgi and Cajal (Scientifica, Neurowire)
note: Excerpt: Golgi backed the reticular theory, which held that the nervous system was one continuous network; his Nobel lecture again emphasised it.

sentence: Santiago Ramón y Cajal saw separate cells.
claim: Santiago Ramón y Cajal argued, using Golgi's own stain, that neurons are discrete cells that communicate at specialised junctions (the neuron doctrine).
source_title: Meet the Nobels: Golgi and Cajal (Scientifica, Neurowire)
note: Excerpt: Cajal provided evidence that neurons are discrete cells that communicate through specialized junctions.

sentence: In nineteen oh six they shared a Nobel Prize, still disagreeing.
claim: Golgi and Cajal shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine; in their Nobel lectures Golgi defended the reticular theory and Cajal refuted it.
source_title: Meet the Nobels: Golgi and Cajal (Scientifica, Neurowire)
note: Excerpt: they shared the prize but disagreed; Golgi's lecture emphasised the reticular theory and Cajal respectfully refuted it.

sentence: Electron microscopes settled it in the nineteen fifties: there's a gap.
claim: Electron micrographs from 1954–55 (Palay and Palade; De Robertis and Bennett) showed the pre- and postsynaptic membranes separated by a cleft, confirming that neurons are separate cells.
source_title: Palay, Palade and the synapse (Journal of Cell Biology, 2005 retrospective; De Robertis & Bennett 1955, Palay & Palade 1955)
note: Excerpts: Palade and Palay's early electron micrographs 'weighed in definitively' on the neuron-doctrine debate; De Robertis and Bennett (1955) describe membranes separated by an intermembranal space of 100–150 Å (10–15 nm). Electron microscopy later showed a plasma membrane enclosing each neuron (Scientifica).

sentence: The signal can't cross it as electricity.
claim: At a chemical synapse the electrical signal does not pass to the next cell directly; it is converted into the release of a chemical neurotransmitter. (Electrical synapses, where current passes through gap junctions, also exist.)
note: Excerpt (StatPearls): chemical synapses transmit via neurotransmitter across the cleft; electrical synapses also exist. The picture is a chemical synapse; bible §9 asks for 'most' (said in episode 3's tease and on screen here).

sentence: So calcium floods the tip, bubbles of chemical messenger burst, and the message drifts across.
claim: When the action potential reaches the terminal, voltage-gated calcium channels open and calcium entry triggers synaptic vesicles to fuse with the membrane and release neurotransmitter.
note: Excerpt: depolarization opens voltage-gated calcium channels; calcium entry drives vesicles to fuse with the presynaptic membrane. 'Burst' = fuse and release (exocytosis); 'floods' is plain speech for the calcium influx.

sentence: So calcium floods the tip, bubbles of chemical messenger burst, and the message drifts across.
claim: Neurotransmitter is stored in synaptic vesicles; once released it diffuses across the synaptic cleft and binds receptors on the next cell.
source_title: Purves et al., Neuroscience 2nd ed., Neurotransmitter release from synaptic vesicles (NCBI Bookshelf NBK11166)
note: Bible S15; excerpt: neurotransmitters are stored in synaptic vesicles and released by exocytosis. JoVE: they diffuse across the cleft and bind postsynaptic receptors. 'Drifts' = diffuses.

sentence: The crossing takes about a thousandth of a second.
claim: Synaptic transmission adds a delay of about 1 ms (release, diffusion across the cleft, receptor binding).
note: Excerpt: 'approximately one millisecond delay because neurotransmitters must be released from synaptic vesicles, diffuse across the synaptic cleft, and bind to postsynaptic receptors'. Bible S17.

sentence: And these gaps can strengthen with use: one way your brain is thought to learn.
claim: Synapses can strengthen or weaken with activity (synaptic plasticity, e.g. long-term potentiation); this is considered a main cellular mechanism of learning and memory.
source_title: Synaptic plasticity and learning (University of Minnesota, Department of Neuroscience)
note: Excerpt (UMN): synaptic plasticity is the best cellular and molecular model of learning and memory. An NIMH-funded researcher: 'Synaptic plasticity is thought to be a basis of learning and memory'. 'Is thought to' keeps the hedge; reviews note it does not explain every kind of learning.

sentence: So your nerves aren't wired together.
claim: Neurons are separate cells; at chemical synapses they are not physically continuous.
source_title: Meet the Nobels: Golgi and Cajal (Scientifica, Neurowire)
note: As c5 and c7 (electron microscopy showed each neuron enclosed by its own membrane). Electrical synapses join some cells through gap junctions; 'wired together' refers to the continuous web Golgi proposed.

sentence: They talk across gaps, in chemicals.
claim: Most signalling between neurons is chemical, across synaptic clefts.
note: As c8; 'talk' is a metaphor for synaptic transmission.

sentence: Meanwhile, as you watched, you took about fifteen breaths.
claim: A normal resting breathing rate for adults is about 12–20 breaths a minute; the tally uses 15 a minute.
source_title: Respiratory rate: a vital sign (American Lung Association)
note: Excerpt: normal respiratory rate for a healthy adult at rest is 12 to 20 breaths per minute. The tally is 15/60 × t from frame 0; the line lands near 60 s, about 15 (computed). At 12–20 a minute the same span gives 12–20, so 'about fifteen' is an estimate for the viewer.

sentence: Each was ordered by a nerve, across a gap like this one.
claim: Each breath in is driven by the phrenic nerve making the diaphragm contract; nerve and muscle meet at a synapse, the neuromuscular junction.
source_title: Anatomy, thorax, phrenic nerves (StatPearls, NCBI Bookshelf NBK513325; title as excerpted)
note: Excerpt (StatPearls, phrenic nerve): it provides the diaphragm's complete motor innervation; its activation makes the diaphragm contract with inspiration. Bio-protocol excerpt: the neuromuscular junction is the specialized synapse by which motor neurons control skeletal muscle. 'Like this one': a chemical synapse (it uses acetylcholine), not identical to the brain synapse drawn.
